summary.headline: Kamat Hotels Q2 FY27 EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 22 crore, margin up 13 pts to 26% on revenue of Rs 86 crore (+12%).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs 86 crore and EBITDA rose 131% to Rs 22 crore, with margin at 26%, while PAT turned to Rs 5 crore from a Rs 2 crore loss a year earlier. H1 revenue was Rs 179 crore (+11%), EBITDA above Rs 50 crore (+67%) at 28% margin, and PAT Rs 15 crore. Same-store revenue rose 31% after excluding IRA Mumbai, Orchid Shimla and IRA Bhavnagar. Net debt to EBITDA fell to 0.23x from 0.52x, and Rs 30 crore of Axis Finance debt was repaid after quarter end. Management guided to a stronger H2 and a FY30 expansion plan of 31 properties and 3,000 keys.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of Rs 2 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Portfolio (occupancy and ADR)
segments.commentary: Portfolio occupancy rose from 50% to 58% while ADR was flat at about 3% growth; RevPAR up about 20% per management. Pune Orchid revenue grew 32%.

segments.name: IRA by Orchid
segments.commentary: Weaker ARR and RevPAR, mainly because IRA Mumbai (high occupancy, good rate) left the portfolio after lease ended 31 March 2026. Excluding IRA Mumbai, RevPAR was Rs 2,337 in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 2,477 in Q2 FY26; H1 Rs 2,472 vs Rs 2,423 (wording as stated in call).

segments.name: New properties (Bhavnagar, Rishikesh)
segments.commentary: Both show negative EBITDA in H1 but management called the amount insignificant; positive EBITDA expected in the next two quarters. Stabilisation takes about one year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 to be the strongest half, with revenue and EBITDA growth above last year's H2 and continued rate and occupancy gains.
Q2 is typically 60-65% of annual business; management expects FY27 to be robust, citing an encouraging October and a strong second half of November.
Indicative: if H2 EBITDA is 60% of the full year, FY27 EBITDA could cross Rs 130-135 crore (FY26 was about Rs 100 crore). Management said it does not want to give forward-looking numbers.
Net debt to be zero by year-end FY27, per the CFO.
FY30 (KHIL 3.0): 31 properties (from 24), 11 states (from 10), 3,000+ keys (from 1,900+), portfolio ARR from about Rs 6,000 to about Rs 8,000 (+33%).
Upcoming openings: Gwalior (Dec/Jan, leased), Dwarka and Nashik (managed; Dwarka about 250-266 keys); Rishikesh and Dehradun later; pipeline about 620 keys across seven properties.
capex_capacity: Pipeline about 620 keys across seven properties; expansion to be within existing states unless financially attractive.
Management model is a flat 6% of top line; lease or revenue-share deals only for properties of roughly 80-100 rooms, management contracts from about 40-45 rooms.

CFO estimates about Rs 750 crore cumulative EBITDA over five years (about Rs 600 crore after tax available for growth) and about Rs 1,000 crore total expansion capacity including debt headroom, on a lower-side basis.
Electric kitchens and an all-EV hotel fleet were capex-heavy decisions that management says helped during LPG/PNG disruption.
demand_pricing: Q2 demand came mainly from corporate for business hotels and leisure for leisure properties; MICE demand described as intact.
Goa (Orchid Passaros) showed strong demand, with a high share of foreign guests.
Wedding season weaker than last year but supportive of weekday and weekend demand.
Management said the focus is on RevPAR over ADR; rates to rise as occupancy picks up, with Pune Orchid ADR expected to jump in Q3 and Q4.
Ayodhya occupancy took a small hit in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 26% EBITDA margin and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: ADR flat at about 3% but occupancy rose 50% to 58%; higher volume with fixed costs drove margin gains, plus Pune (revenue +32%), Bhubaneswar and cost efficiencies. Management said margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 revenue growth driven by occupancy, ARR or new properties?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: H2 is the strongest period; rates and occupancy are both expected to rise, lifting top line and EBITDA. No split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is IRA by Orchid weaker on ARR and RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman: new hotels dilute averages and mature markets such as Sambhaji Nagar and Nashik are growing slowly. CFO: the drop is mainly IRA Mumbai leaving the portfolio; ex-Mumbai RevPAR was broadly flat, with a small Ayodhya dip.

qa_highlights.question: When will new properties such as Bhavnagar and Rishikesh stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: about one year to stabilise; H1 EBITDA is slightly negative but not significant; positive EBITDA expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion pipeline and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman declined to name specifics, citing negotiations; expansion limited to existing states with internal norms. CFO gave indicative numbers: FY27 EBITDA of about Rs 130-135 crore if H2 is 60%, and about Rs 1,000 crore of expansion capacity over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Which models will expansion use and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman: management contracts at a flat 6% of top line (GOP-linked fees dropped), above 40-45 rooms; leases only for 80-100+ room hotels because GST at 18% is a cost for smaller hotels; revenue share as an exception.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the royalty payable to Plaza on the Mumbai hotel up from 3% to 5%, and will it be cut, given the interest-free deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: royalty is about Rs 9 crore a year at 6% on Rs 150 crore revenue, compared with about Rs 35 crore finance cost on a Rs 300-350 crore land value; a merger with the promoter entity is being evaluated but is not yet decided. Chairman: the 1994 arrangement is not to be changed, and the board will decide.

qa_highlights.question: How did demand and ARR evolve across segments, and when will rates improve?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: outlook robust; Q2 demand was corporate-led for business hotels and leisure for leisure properties. Rate levels depend on micro-market; RevPAR is the focus, with occupancy pushed in Q2 and rates to follow.

risks_watch: Royalty to promoter entity Plaza raised from 3% to 5% for the Mumbai hotel in 2024; minority shareholder concerns and a possible merger are unresolved.
GST structure raises costs for smaller hotels and constrains lease economics; management says industry representations are unlikely to succeed.
Diwali timing shifted into mid-November, so November may be weaker than last year; wedding season weaker than last year.
Sustainability of the 26% margin and the ~3% ADR growth; Q3 and Q4 ADR jump needs to show up in numbers.
Ramp-up of Bhavnagar, Rishikesh and Dwarka/Nashik/Gwalior openings, and whether H2 EBITDA meets the indicated Rs 130-135 crore FY27 level.
Management said a call-quality issue meant some participants could not be heard; audio gaps mean a few questions went unanswered.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, deleveraging and H2, with specific numbers. Evasive on pipeline names and on the Plaza royalty and merger question, which was deferred to the board.
key_quotes: This was not just a growth but this was a decisive turnaround in profitability.
Our net debt to EBITDA it was 0.23x versus 0.52x as of last quarter, more than halved in just one quarter.
We need basically properties which are in the range of 80 to 100 for us to take on particularly lease.
In management, it does not matter. Even if it is a 40 room hotel because we charge a flat 6%.

adds.what: Rishikesh and Dehradun properties (timing later), part of ~620-key pipeline across seven properties
FY30 target of 31 properties and 3,000+ keys (from 24 properties, ~1,900 keys)

growth.why: Management guides a stronger H2 and FY27 EBITDA of Rs 130-135 crore if H2 is 60% of the year (vs ~Rs 100 crore FY26), backed by occupancy gains from 50% to 58%, rate increases expected at Pune Orchid, and openings at Gwalior, Dwarka and Nashik, though the FY30 plan of 31 properties and 3,000 keys has no firm timeline beyond FY30 and management declined to give forward numbers.
